addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text **moves** here
(never copied; one home per text). The picked-up task is a
`###` heading; a multi-cycle program adds one level, where the
program is the `###` and its current stage a `####` (headings
give the current work durable anchors, which numbered Todo
entries can't). The problem overview is followed by the
"plan", a bulleted list of the development "ladder". Each
rung is prepended with its commit reference, a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then
backfilled to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as
the chores As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

### Refactor: typed jj facade -> jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", ...)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init: stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

Program ladder in **straight trunk order**, one bullet per commit that lands on the branch, so
reading it top to bottom is reading `git log --first-parent`. `refactor:` entries are the
program's rungs, one per cycle (adjacent stages consolidated 2026-07-24; titles are the
anticipated close-out titles; unshipped versions are provisional, since jj-lib may split into
two cycles). Every other prefix is a cycle that landed between rungs and belongs to none of
them: the `docs:` interludes, and the `style:` sweep at 0.78.2, which was a `## Todo` cycle
rather than program work. Every shipped `refactor:` ref points at a close-out commit published
via the long-lived `refactor-vc-x1` bookmark (merge-only while it ran; fully merged into main
and deleted 2026-08-03 under jj.md's long-lived bookmark discipline). Cycles after that
deletion, 0.78.2 first, land directly on `main`.

The order is load-bearing: a
trapezoid's `<base>` is the parent of its own first rung, not
the previous close-out, so 0.78.0 bases on 0.77.4. Taking the
close-out instead swallows the interludes into the merge's
ladder side, which already bit at 0.76.0, whose base was the
0.75.1 interlude. See
[the recipe](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe).

# Chores-16

Continuation of `chores-15.md` (closed after `0.78.0`, the jj-lib migration close-out; the
`0.78.1` instruction-set interlude between the files is recorded in its TODO.md program-ladder
rung and commit body). This file covers `0.78.2` onward, back on `main` with the refactor
program's long-lived bookmark retired and the 20260803 baseline pin set in force.

Reference numbering is file-local; see
[`agent-data/notes.md`](../../agent-data/notes.md#reference-numbering); chores-16 starts at
`[1]`.

## Table of Contents

- [style: typeable punctuation + line-width source sweep](#style-typeable-punctuation--line-width-source-sweep)

## style: typeable punctuation + line-width source sweep

- [[1]] 0.78.2 style: typeable punctuation + line-width source sweep

`src/` + `tests/` predate the typeable-punctuation rule and code.md's <=100-col comment wrap:
863 banned-character sites across 63 files and 60 overlong lines at pickup. A single-commit
cycle (wink's call at the opening review: the sweep is one homogeneous transformation, so a
ladder would checkpoint nothing a review gate and jj's op log don't already cover).

- the four named characters went to zero: `->` and `...` by mechanical replace, the 708 em
  dashes each given their structural decision (colon for term-elaboration, comma for
  continuation, parentheses for asides, sentence splits for contrasts), converted by four
  parallel lesser-model agents on disjoint file batches and audited after
- the sweep surfaced four *more* untypeable species the ban list does not name: `=>` was
  written `⇒` (13 sites), the config/show output drew rules with `─` (56), plus one `≥` and
  one U+2212 minus; all converted, output tests updated in the same pass (see the dogfood
  finding on the enumeration)
- the ellipsis in `truncate_chars` was load-bearing: appending one-char `…` kept truncated
  gists at cap+1, and the mechanical `...` conversion broke the length test; the function now
  reserves room for the suffix and stays within `max` (contract tightened, test to `<= CAP`)
- `config_cmd` section headers (`# ── x ──`) and `show`'s separator rule are user-visible
  output; they render as `-` runs now, and the README's config samples were regenerated from
  the installed binary so the docs match what the code emits
- line width: string literals split with backslash continuation (content byte-identical),
  comments re-wrapped, trailing `// OK:` comments moved above their statement where wrapping
  was awkward; exempt as literal rows: the JSONL fixture strings in the transcript /
  bot-session tests, and comment URLs

Riding in the same commit: the cycle records, the Done-retirement sweep of four
refactor-program entries into done.md, the `0.78.1` ladder-ref backfill, and the first
generic-custom.md-test findings logged in [notes/dogfood.md](../dogfood.md).

### Delegation notes

Four Sonnet agents converted the em-dash batches and a fifth did the line-width pass; two
incidents worth remembering when delegating sweeps:

- one batch agent "corrected" scope creep it thought it saw, reverting 29 already-converted
  arrows back to `→` because it compared against a pre-sweep baseline; caught by the
  post-batch character audit. A delegated sweep needs the invariant stated as "the end state
  is X", not "convert only Y": agents infer baselines
- the line-width agent first placed the continuation break-space after the backslash, which
  Rust strips with the leading whitespace, silently corrupting a fixture string; its own
  `cargo test` run caught it. String splits verify by test, not by eye

# References

[1]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/a8b43a18999e "a8b43a18999ece30e7b807650ba45eb9b236ebdc"

# Mailbox: vc-x1

Protocol in [MESSAGES.md](../MESSAGES.md): handle, then delete the entry; delete the file when
empty.

## 2026-08-03 from iiac-perf (f5) + wink: adopt jj revsets (docs + CLI), mailbox config, 3 fixes

iiac-perf's review of the 20260803 baseline, plus two items from wink's session with it today;
the rest of the review (drop-list verdict, adoption sequencing, tier-2 views) lands at today's
discussion. The headline is a decision wink made today, not yet discussed with you: the
family's house revset convention was a mistake, and jj's native semantics should be adopted,
docs and CLI both, ASAP.

- **Adopt jj's revset semantics; retire the house convention** (wink, 2026-08-03)
  - the trigger: jj.md's new Revsets primer and jj-tips.md gloss `X..` as "descendants of X
    excluding X"; in jj itself `x..` is `~::x` (everything not an ancestor of x), which on a
    repo with parked branches includes unrelated commits. The primer documents raw `-r`
    arguments, so the gloss feeds real `jj rebase` / `jj abandon` target choices
  - the CLI: vc-x1 currently converts house-convention revsets to jj's when issuing jj
    commands; it should stop converting and pass revsets to jj verbatim, so one dialect
    exists and `jj help -k revsets` is the single authority
  - cutover care: the two dialects share syntax, so the flip is silent; sweep the repos'
    durable text for `..`-form revsets in the same cycle. iiac-perf's protocol usages are all
    `..@`, which means the same thing in both dialects, so its sweep is small; jj-tips.md's
    tutorial transcripts (~lines 282-289, 334-337) are the real rewrites
  - docs rewrite: teach `::` as the primary, symmetric operator (`::x` ancestors, `x::`
    descendants, `x::y` the path); present `..` as git-compatible set subtraction with a
    warning on the open-ended forms; add one history line noting vc-x1 formerly translated a
    house convention, so old transcripts stay decodable
- **Mailbox parameters belong in `.vc-config.toml`, not custom.md** (from wink's
  byte-identical-instruction-files goal, 2026-08-03; a discussion item, not a decision)
  - the goal: custom.md generic at birth, so a new repo is byte-identical to the payload from
    its first commit and any later diff is a real customization
  - the blocker: custom.md currently carries the member name and the template repository's
    path, and AGENTS.md's acquaint-time practice depends on both
  - the fix: those are environment configuration, not instruction text, and `.vc-config.toml`
    already holds that species of fact (`other-repo = ".claude"`, a per-checkout relative
    path) while sitting outside the pinned set, so moving them costs byte-identity nothing
  - the pinned practice then assumes no layout: check your mailbox at acquaint if this project
    participates in a message community, whose location and your member name come from
    `.vc-config.toml`; absent config means no community, a free no-op. Non-participation
    becomes the silent default rather than an override, which is backwards today
  - why layout-free matters (wink): the sibling arrangement of the family's repos is a local
    convention, not something an outside adopter should inherit, nor one we are committed to
    keeping. iiac-perf's earlier suggestion to pin it as a family-wide rule is withdrawn
- **custom.md skeleton: stale validation step number**: work/custom.md points Full validation
  at "per-commit checklist step 4", but the renumbered checklist has "Close the records" at 4
  and validation at 5
- **prose.md: two lines over its own <=100 limit**: line 19 (106 cols) and line 71 (134 cols),
  both from the 0802/0803 amendment splices; a rewrap fixes both
- **versioning.md: "this project" narration in a pinned file**: "This project adopted the
  convention 2026-07-23 (during 0.75.0)" reads as the reader's own history; name vc-x1 or
  drop the sentence (the vc-x1-dev example itself is fine as an example)

Done when: the docs fixes land in the template payload (jj-tips.md included for the revset
item), the CLI's revset pass-through is tracked vc-x1-side (its cycle is yours to scope), and
the mailbox-config move has your view on the schema, which it needs before the pinned practice
can be reworded.

## 2026-07-31 from wink + iiac-perf (f5): template restructure landed; old repos await your discussion

`vc-x1-template` (this repo) is the new template + coordination point: payload split into
`work/` + `work.claude/` so init copies only payload (the old flat layout copied discussion
files into new repos; see public exhibit https://github.com/winksaville/test1). Invocation:
`vc-x1 init <name> --use-template <path>/vc-x1-template/work` (single arg; the `<CODE>.claude`
concat default finds `work.claude/`).

- disposition of `vc-x1-work-repo-template` (+ its `.claude`) and `vc-x1-bot-repo-template` is
  deliberately untouched, pending wink discussing it with you; their working copies were left
  exactly as found
- CLI ideas triaged 2026-08-02 into vc-x1's `notes/todo-backlog.md` #46 ("init template
  ergonomics"); the remaining open item is the old repos' fate

Done when: you and wink have decided the old repos' fate.

442	### A subcommand, not a flag on push
443	
444	Decided 2026-07-28, replacing the earlier `push --merge
445	[<base>]` design:
446	
447	- **`push` keeps an invariant worth stating: it never
448	  produces a merge.** A mode flag would rewire the stage
449	  sequence from inside, which is the classic
450	  shape-changing-flag smell; a separate verb names the act.
451	- Three open questions dissolve: mutual exclusion with a
452	  future `--squash` (separate verbs can't conflict),
453	  "no state-file growth, re-passed on resume" (nothing to
454	  re-pass), and clap's optional-value footgun, where `--merge
455	  [<base>]` needs `--merge=<rev>` to disambiguate from a
456	  following positional, where a subcommand takes `<bookmark>`
457	  positionally and `--base <rev>` as an ordinary flag.
458	- Named for the `<shape>-push` spelling `squash-push` already
459	  uses. The parallel is the *name*, not the semantics, since
460	  `squash-push` is a bot-repo operation. Help text opens with
461	  the bridge for git readers: a non-fast-forward merge, which
462	  this project calls a trapezoid. "no-ff" is not introduced
463	  as a third spelling.
464	- **Duplication is answered by extraction, not by copying.**
465	  `push` and `trapezoid-push` share nearly everything
466	  (preflight, both approval gates, message composition,
467	  commit-work, commit-bot, bookmark-set, push-work, the bot
468	  squash) and differ by one inserted step. The shared
469	  pipeline moves into its own module both call; each
470	  subcommand is a thin front-end over it. The stateless-push
471	  cycle shrinks that pipeline first, which is what makes the
472	  extraction cheap.
473	- **A backend `trait` is the right shape only when a second
474	  backend exists.** If a git (or other VCS) implementation
475	  ever appears, converting these concepts to traits with two
476	  implementations is the natural move and worth doing then.
477	  Today we are committed to jj, and a trait with one
478	  implementation buys indirection and no abstraction.
479	
480	- The merge itself is trivial in-process: a two-parent commit
481	  in one transaction; no conflicts possible since the base is
482	  an ancestor of the tip.
483	- Doing it **in-flight** (see the stage placement below) is
484	  strictly better than the manual procedure: nothing is
485	  published in the interim shape, so there is no unreachable
486	  SHA, no sideways bookmark move, and no backfill embargo
487	  window. That wart is an artifact of the flag not existing.
488	- Teach `validate-desc` + the push sanity verifiers the new
489	  legal shape (two parents, N ochids).
490	- Assert the parent count **after** the rebase rather than

492	  verification step, promoted to a code check.

- **`push` keeps an invariant worth stating: it never
  produces a merge.** A mode flag would rewire the stage
  sequence from inside, which is the classic
  shape-changing-flag smell; a separate verb names the act.
- Three open questions dissolve: mutual exclusion with a
  future `--squash` (separate verbs can't conflict),
  "no state-file growth, re-passed on resume" (nothing to
  re-pass), and clap's optional-value footgun, where `--merge
  [<base>]` needs `--merge=<rev>` to disambiguate from a
  following positional, where a subcommand takes `<bookmark>`
  positionally and `--base <rev>` as an ordinary flag.
- Named for the `<shape>-push` spelling `squash-push` already
  uses. The parallel is the *name*, not the semantics, since
  `squash-push` is a bot-repo operation. Help text opens with
  the bridge for git readers: a non-fast-forward merge, which
  this project calls a trapezoid. "no-ff" is not introduced
  as a third spelling.
- **Duplication is answered by extraction, not by copying.**
  `push` and `trapezoid-push` share nearly everything
  (preflight, both approval gates, message composition,
  commit-work, commit-bot, bookmark-set, push-work, the bot
  squash) and differ by one inserted step. The shared
  pipeline moves into its own module both call; each
  subcommand is a thin front-end over it. The stateless-push
  cycle shrinks that pipeline first, which is what makes the
  extraction cheap.
- **A backend `trait` is the right shape only when a second
  backend exists.** If a git (or other VCS) implementation
  ever appears, converting these concepts to traits with two
  implementations is the natural move and worth doing then.
  Today we are committed to jj, and a trait with one
  implementation buys indirection and no abstraction.

- The merge itself is trivial in-process: a two-parent commit
  in one transaction; no conflicts possible since the base is
  an ancestor of the tip.
- Doing it **in-flight** (see the stage placement below) is
  strictly better than the manual procedure: nothing is
  published in the interim shape, so there is no unreachable
  SHA, no sideways bookmark move, and no backfill embargo
  window. That wart is an artifact of the flag not existing.
- Teach `validate-desc` + the push sanity verifiers the new
  legal shape (two parents, N ochids).
- Assert the parent count **after** the rebase rather than
  trusting jj not to simplify the edge: the manual recipe's
  verification step, promoted to a code check.
- Status: the 0.72.0 attempt to pull this stage forward
  paused on the `support-trapezoid-commits` bookmark and is
  now abandoned as a version; see the
  [parked-branch disposition](#parked-0720-branch-disposition-quarry-not-base)
  (its ladder plan remains the template for this cycle).
  The stage runs here, in program order, on the refactored
  internals, with body-intro validation as its first rung.
  The former enabler Todo "vc-x1 push: pause point between
  commit and publish stages" was retired unimplemented,
  because native merge support supersedes the pause.

  first commit), `--base <rev>` on the subcommand:
  - branch style (task on a feature bookmark, target
    sitting at the base): base defaults to the target

Agreed on #3, and for a stronger reason than "it's the feature I want": **0.79.0 is the last rung on the program ladder**, so shipping it is what lets the `## In Progress` section close. #1 is process debt already staged for the iiac-perf review, and #2 only pays out at the next jj-lib bump. Neither blocks a release; the program hanging open does.

Some things I turned up that change the plan's assumptions.

## The parked branch is not a quarry worth mining

`support-trapezoid-commits` still exists at `7694fce7 refactor: extract push/state.rs`. That extraction is built around **`push/state.rs`, the state file 0.77.0 deleted**. The disposition note says "try `jj rebase` onto the tip, redo if it conflicts badly" - but this isn't a conflict problem, it's that the thing being extracted no longer exists. Four cycles of churn (DRY facade, facade owns topology, stateless push, jj-lib) have gone over that code since.

My read: skip the rebase attempt entirely, treat the diff as at most a shape reference for the front-end/pipeline split, and delete the bookmark at cycle open rather than at the end. That saves a rung of pointless history gymnastics. Worth also asking what `config-discoverability` is still doing in the bookmark list.

## Closing the program needs more than the rung

Three loose ends in `refactor-20260716.md` that the TODO ladder does not cover:

1. **Stage: por -> dual conversion** is still in the program doc, marked "last on purpose", but the ladder stops at 0.79.0. Closing the program means deciding explicitly: retire it to `## Todo` / backlog as its own future cycle. I think that's right (it is init/setup work, not push-pipeline work, and nothing about the release depends on it) but it should be a stated decision, not a silent drop.
2. **Stage: Access rule** owes ARCHITECTURE.md the end-state description. It is currently stale in a way that matters for a release: `src/jj.rs` is still described as "the typed facade over `jj` subprocess queries" with "Mutations still spawn `jj` at their call sites until the refactor program's jj-lib migration stage moves both in-process" - which shipped at 0.78.0. Same section still says `-s code|bot` where the scope is now `work`.
3. **bugs.md #7** (`push --body` rejects a body whose first character is `-`) is exactly what body-intro validation resolves. It should be retired by this cycle, not left sitting.

## Proposed ladder

- **0.79.0-0** cycle open: chores-16 section, delete the parked bookmark, abandon the 0.72.0-0 chore commit
- **0.79.0-1** body-intro validation: small, self-contained, closes bugs.md #7, and lands the papercut fix early where it can be dogfooded for the rest of the cycle
- **0.79.0-2** pipeline extraction, no behavior change: shared module, `push` becomes a thin front-end over it, existing push tests are the gate
- **0.79.0-3** `trapezoid-push`: the merge in-flight after commit-bot and before bookmark-set, both base-inference styles, preconditions, parent-count asserted **after** the rebase
- **0.79.0-4** `validate-desc` + the push sanity verifiers learn the two-parent / N-ochid shape
- **0.79.0-5** close-out: README + docs ride-along, ARCHITECTURE.md access rule, program retired from `## In Progress`

`push.rs` is 796 lines with tests already split into `src/push/`, so -2 should be genuinely cheap the way stateless-push promised.

The tempting move at -5 is to publish the close-out **with `trapezoid-push` itself**. I'm for it - it is the honest dogfood and the manual four-step recipe remains the documented fallback if it misbehaves - but that is your call at the push, not mine, and it should be a deliberate decision rather than something we drift into.

## One push-back on sequencing, not on the choice

You said "released". The mailbox carries wink's 2026-08-03 decision that the CLI should **stop translating revsets** and pass them to jj verbatim. That is a user-visible semantics change on shared syntax, which means it is silent: the same string means something different before and after. Shipping a release that still translates makes the first public version teach the house dialect, and fixing it afterward is a breaking change to a released tool.

It does not need to come before 0.79.0. But I would slot it as 0.80.0 and **before** the release tag, not after. It also looks small: `ARCHITECTURE.md` points at `DotSpec` / `..`-notation parsing in `src/common`, so this is mostly a deletion plus a durable-text sweep.

## What I need from you

- Confirm por -> dual retires out of the program (my recommendation) rather than holding it open.
- Confirm the revset cutover lands before the release tag, so I can note it on the ladder now.
- The validation commands, still. `custom.md` is the bare skeleton, so I have no pinned source for what "validate the artifact" runs.

**The plain version:** #3 is the right pick and it closes the program. The old parked branch is dead weight - redo the work instead of rebasing it. Add ARCHITECTURE.md and the por -> dual disposition to the cycle so the program actually closes. And do the revset change before you tag the release, not after, because afterward it becomes a breaking change.

175	restates the other.

194	
195	The first content under a chores section header is the **as-built ladder**: one rung per
196	commit the section records, in landing order, each rung carrying its own `[N]` citation slot.

198	one-rung ladder whose rung is the bare `X.Y.Z` close-out:

200	```
201	## refactor: extract config loader

207	```

209	- The rung form is `- [[N]] X.Y.Z[-n] <title>`, with no `(current)` / `(done)` markers:
210	  as-built implies done (the in-flight markers live in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`).

214	  [Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)), **double-bracketed** so the brackets render.

217	  `# References` definition puts the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full

227	  `git show <40-hex>` works in any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a database,
228	  say) gets the canonical identifier.
229	
230	**Timing.** A commit's SHA isn't stable until it lands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a
231	long-lived release/patch branch), because a rebase or squash rewrites it on the way. A commit
232	can't record its own SHA, so the fill lands one push later: every rung opens with the literal

236	[Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill).

238	Sections that predate this convention keep their `Commits:` lines; the ladder form applies
239	going forward.
240

242	
243	Each `chores-NN.md` carries a `## Table of Contents` section between the file intro and the

246	
247	- Entries are title-only, with no version and no `[N]` refs, so the TOC never needs backfill:
248	  the TOC navigates, the section's as-built ladder records.
249	- Append the entry when the section opens; the entry text participates in the same last-edit
250	  title sync as the section header and the `## Done` entry.
251	- Design `###` subsections stay out of the TOC.
252	- Files predating the convention gain a TOC opportunistically, not on a schedule.

source of truth lives here; [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this
before editing a notes file.

Universal file, pinned to the template repository; do not edit here. Project overrides go in
[custom.md](../custom.md).

## File reads: read the slice you need

  [Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)), **double-bracketed** so the brackets render.
  (`[[3]]` shows as a literal `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner `[3]`
  resolves against its `[3]:` definition, and CommonMark / GitHub / VS Code all do this.) The
  `# References` definition puts the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full
  40-hex SHA** in the title slot:

```
[3]: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<12-hex> "<40-hex>"
```

- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short; GitHub / GitLab resolve a unique prefix to
  the canonical commit page (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).
- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous: it survives a repo host change,
  `git show <40-hex>` works in any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a database,
  say) gets the canonical identifier.

**Timing.** A commit's SHA isn't stable until it lands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a
long-lived release/patch branch), because a rebase or squash rewrites it on the way. A commit
can't record its own SHA, so the fill lands one push later: every rung opens with the literal
`[[N]]` placeholder, and each push backfills the rungs of the commits the previous push made
permanent. On a topic branch a section waits until the branch lands. The commit itself is the
record, and `git log --grep "<title>"` finds it. See cycle-protocol
[Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill).

Sections that predate this convention keep their `Commits:` lines; the ladder form applies
going forward.

### Chores file Table of Contents

Each `chores-NN.md` carries a `## Table of Contents` section between the file intro and the
first commit-recording section: one `- [<title>](#<anchor>)` entry per commit-recording `##`
section, in file order.

- Entries are title-only, with no version and no `[N]` refs, so the TOC never needs backfill:
  the TOC navigates, the section's as-built ladder records.
- Append the entry when the section opens; the entry text participates in the same last-edit
  title sync as the section header and the `## Done` entry.
- Design `###` subsections stay out of the TOC.
- Files predating the convention gain a TOC opportunistically, not on a schedule.

#### refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation

The trapezoid close-out is a four-step manual recipe today, and every wart in it is an
artifact of the shape having no command: an interim published shape, a sideways bookmark move,
a backfill embargo window. `vc-x1 trapezoid-push` makes it first-party, as a **subcommand**
rather than a flag on `push` (decided 2026-07-28), so `push` keeps a stateable invariant: it
never produces a merge. Body-intro validation rides as the first rung, turning jj's opaque
`-m "-..."` arg-parse failure ([bugs.md](notes/bugs.md) #7) into a clear error naming the
offending line. Design in
[trapezoid close-out](notes/refactor-20260716.md#stage-trapezoid-close-out) and
[push body-intro validation](notes/refactor-20260716.md#stage-push-body-intro-validation).

Duplication is answered by extraction, not by copying: `push` and `trapezoid-push` share
preflight, both approval gates, message composition, commit-work, commit-bot, bookmark-set,
push-work and the bot squash, and differ by one inserted step. The stateless-push cycle already
shrank that pipeline, which is what makes the extraction cheap.

- [[N]] 0.79.0-0 chore: open the trapezoid-push cycle (current)
  - rides the pending records work: the `0.78.0` / `0.78.2` as-built backfills, the two
    2026-08-03 dogfood entries, and the `## Done` retirement sweep
  - the parked `support-trapezoid-commits` bookmark is deleted here rather than mined: its
    one commit extracts `push/state.rs`, the module `0.77.0` deleted, so the quarry has no
    ore. The `0.72.0-0` chore commit is abandoned with it
- [[N]] 0.79.0-1 feat: push body-intro validation
  - self-contained and first on purpose: it retires [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md) #7 and is then
    dogfooded by every remaining rung's own push
- [[N]] 0.79.0-2 refactor: extract the shared push pipeline
  - no behavior change; `push` becomes a thin front-end over the extracted module and the
    existing push tests are the gate
- [[N]] 0.79.0-3 feat: verifiers accept the trapezoid shape
  - `validate-desc` and the push sanity verifiers learn two parents and N ochids, before the
    command that produces that shape exists, so the next rung's output validates on arrival
- [[N]] 0.79.0-4 feat: vc-x1 trapezoid-push
  - the merge in-flight, after commit-bot and before bookmark-set; both base styles (branch
    infers, main requires explicit `--base`); preconditions checked; parent count asserted
    **after** the rebase rather than trusting jj not to simplify the edge
  - `README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` ride this commit, the one that makes the subcommand
    real: the user-facing section leading with `trapezoid-push`, and the access rule restated
    now that mutations are in-process (`src/jj.rs` is still described as a subprocess facade,
    and the scope selector as `-s code|bot`)
- [[N]] 0.79.0 refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation
  - bookkeeping, plus the program retirement; shape chosen at push time, where using
    `trapezoid-push` on its own close-out is the honest dogfood and the manual recipe is the
    documented fallback

Done, and nothing is committed. `TODO.md` only.

## What changed

**Todo #3 moved to `## In Progress`** as a `####` stage under the program `###` (one home per text: the old entry is gone, not copied). The program rung is marked `(current)`, with a note that this close-out retires the program block.

**`por -> dual conversion` created as Todo #4**, carrying why it left the program: init/setup work, its "last on purpose" dependencies (facade topology, in-process init) have both shipped, and nothing else in the program needed it. Rank flagged as provisional. List renumbered and `validate-todo` passes: 20 entries, all sequential.

## The ladder proposal

You floated a single step. I don't think this one compresses that far - 0.78.2 was one homogeneous transformation, this is five different kinds of change - but I did compress it from what I sketched last turn:

| Rung | |
|---|---|
| `0.79.0-0` | `chore: open the trapezoid-push cycle` |
| `0.79.0-1` | `feat: push body-intro validation` |
| `0.79.0-2` | `refactor: extract the shared push pipeline` |
| `0.79.0-3` | `feat: verifiers accept the trapezoid shape` |
| `0.79.0-4` | `feat: vc-x1 trapezoid-push` |
| `0.79.0` | `refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation` |

Three choices worth your eye:

- **`-1` goes first** so bugs #7 is retired early and then dogfooded by every later rung's own push. Free confidence.
- **`-3` before `-4`**: teach `validate-desc` and the sanity verifiers the two-parent / N-ochid shape *before* the command that emits it, so `-4`'s output validates on arrival instead of landing broken and being fixed after. The cost is one rung where the verifiers accept a shape nothing produces yet, testable with a hand-built fixture.
- **ARCHITECTURE.md rides `-4`, not the close-out.** Close-out is bookkeeping-only by protocol, and the access rule wants restating on the same commit that makes the subcommand real - alongside the README section, which the design already pins there. It also pays the jj-lib program's outstanding doc debt: `src/jj.rs` is still described as a subprocess facade with "Mutations still spawn `jj`", and the scope selector as `-s code|bot` rather than `work`.

`-0` also deletes `support-trapezoid-commits` rather than mining it, and abandons the `0.72.0-0` chore commit.

## Two things I found while editing

**The ASCII check is not as clean as I implied.** `grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]'` over several files at once dropped `TODO.md`'s hits entirely; run alone, `TODO.md` has 7. Most are `↔` used as a relation glyph (`code↔bot`, `rung↔commit`, `por ↔ dual`), one `␠`, and one `## Done` line that is legitimately *quoting* the banned characters. So the dogfood finding needs two amendments: the check must be per-file or `-r`, and the rule needs a quoting exemption. Not fixing it in this cycle unless you want it; it is notes-side, and 0.78.2 deliberately scoped itself to `src/` + `tests/`.

**Bugs #7's phrasing understates it.** It reads as a `--body` parser bug; the design says enforcing a non-dash intro is the *intended* behavior. `-1` should rewrite the bugs entry as it retires it, so the record does not read as if we papered over a parser problem.

## Still open from last turn

- **Validation commands.** Preparation is notes-only so it can skip, but I need them confirmed before `-1`. `custom.md` still points at placeholders.
- **Revset cutover before the release tag** (my suggested 0.80.0). You answered the other three; this one did not get a verdict, and it decides whether I create the Todo now.

1. **Revsets: correct the docs, and decide the `..` positional collision.** From the mailbox
   (iiac-perf + wink, 2026-08-03), whose premise needs correcting before the work is scoped:
   the message says vc-x1 "converts house-convention revsets to jj's when issuing jj commands"
   and should stop. It does not. `common::resolve_revset` hands its string straight to
   `jj_lib::revset::parse`, and every revset vc-x1 composes internally is already `::`-form
   (`{rev}::`, `::{rev}`, `all()`). There is no translation layer to delete.
   - **What is real is a syntax collision, not a translation.** `common::parse_dot_rev` gives
     the read-only query commands (`list`, `show`, `desc`, `validate-desc`, `fix-desc`) a
     house `..` shorthand on their `REVISION` positional, where `x..`, `..x` and `..x..` mean
     "walk this many ancestors / descendants around `x`". It is a display-range shorthand
     parsed into counts and stripped before anything reaches jj, so it is not a revset at all.
     But it spells `..` and means something else than jj's `..`, which is the hazard the
     mailbox is really pointing at.
   - So the decision is a **CLI syntax** one, not a pass-through toggle: retire the house
     shorthand, rename it, or keep it and document the collision loudly. That decision has
     not been made, which is why this is not a rung inside `0.79.0`.
   - The **docs half is real and unblocked**: jj.md's Revsets primer glosses `X..` as
     "descendants of X excluding X" where jj means `~::x`. That is a pinned file, so it is a
     template proposal rather than a local edit.
   - Reply to the mailbox with the correction first; iiac-perf and wink are both reasoning
     from a model of the code that does not match it.
2. **Notes-side ASCII sweep, after the quoting exemption is settled.** `0.78.2` swept `src/`
   and `tests/` and deliberately left `notes/` and the root docs; `TODO.md` alone has 7
   non-ASCII lines, and `bugs.md`, `transcript-format.md` and `refactor-20260716.md` have
   many more.
   - Blocked on a rule question, which is why it is a Todo and not a rung: one `## Done` line
     legitimately *quotes* the banned characters while recording the cycle that banned them.
     A blanket ASCII rule needs a quoting exemption, or that line becomes unwritable.
   - Most sites are not the four named characters: `↔` used as a relation glyph (`code↔bot`,
     `rung↔commit`, `por ↔ dual`) and one `␠`. Each wants a judgment, not a mechanical
     replace, so it is the same shape as the em-dash pass.
   - **The check itself misreports.** `grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]'` over several file arguments
     at once silently omitted `TODO.md`'s hits; run against `TODO.md` alone it finds all 7.
     Whatever the dogfood finding proposes as the greppable acceptance check must be
     per-file or `-r`, or it will read clean while text is dirty.
3. **commit-description guardrails: exact first bullet in the checklist; hard-rule question.**

     `src/common.rs`, on the `REVISION` positional (and `-r`) of the read-only query commands
     (`list`, `show`, `desc`, `validate-desc`, `fix-desc`). Documented in
     [README](README.md) as "The `..` notation".

     to switch off: `common::resolve_revset` already hands its string verbatim to
     `jj_lib::revset::parse`, and every revset vc-x1 composes internally is already `::`-form
     (`{rev}::`, `::{rev}`, `all()`). The work is deleting the dot shorthand and letting the
     positional *be* a revset, not flipping a translation flag.

     output direction (`x..` puts x at top with older below; `..x` puts x at bottom) and the

     neither. Decide per affordance: a flag, jj's default ordering, or dropped.

     outside rather than buried in a cycle named for something else. Note versioning.md is

Corrected. Todo #1 is rewritten around your demo.

## Where I was wrong, and what survives

Wrong: I concluded "no translation, therefore not the thing the mailbox describes." Your two commands show the house reading is not merely different from jj's, it is **inverted** - `@..` is ancestors here and `~::@` in jj, `..@` is descendants here and ancestors in jj. Both dialects parse, neither errors, and the answers are opposite. That is worse than a collision and the mailbox is right to call it a conversion, because from where the user sits it is one.

What survives is only a scoping note, not an argument: there is no revset-string rewriter to switch off. `resolve_revset` already passes verbatim to `jj_lib::revset::parse`, and vc-x1's internal revsets are already `::`-form. So the work is deleting `parse_dot_rev` / `DotSpec` and letting the positional *be* a revset. I put that in the entry so nobody estimates the cutover as a flag flip.

## The one thing that makes it bigger than a deletion

README `## The .. notation` documents two affordances a bare revset cannot express:

- **output direction**: `x..` puts x at top with older below, `..x` puts x at bottom
- **the `..x..` split budget**: `-n 4` gives 1 descendant, x, 2 ancestors

Delete the shorthand and both vanish. `vc-x1 list '::@' -n 5` gets you the right commits and says nothing about ordering; `..x..` has no single-revset equivalent that also splits the budget. So each needs a decision - a flag, jj's default ordering, or dropped as not worth keeping.

## On `-5`

That is the whole of my remaining objection, and it is weaker than the one I opened with. My recommendation is still a separate cycle, on two grounds:

- **The cycle title would stop describing the cycle.** Hard rule 9 ties the `####` heading, the chores header and the close-out title together, and "refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation" would not cover a breaking revset change. Widening it to carry both makes an unwieldy title for a cycle doing two unrelated things.
- **It is a breaking, user-visible change heading into a release.** It reads better as its own version - a user scanning what changed sees the revset semantics named, rather than finding them inside a cycle named for trapezoid-push.

Related: versioning.md turns out to be silent on what a bump promises a user. It is a cycle-phase scheme, not a compatibility policy. Worth settling before you tag, and noted in the entry.

That said, you lean `-5`, the premise I argued from was wrong, and "fix it sooner" is your call to make. Say the word and I will add it as `0.79.0-5` and retitle the cycle; otherwise it stays Todo #1 and goes out as `0.80.0` before the tag.

The five validation commands from my last message - four full, one fast. That is the only thing blocking me from finishing Preparation.

**The plain version:** you were right, the dialects are inverted and it is a real conversion. The entry now says so. The cutover is a deletion plus two design decisions about output direction and the split budget. content.text:
Verified against your two examples. Direct answers first.

## Example 1: `vc-x1 list ..ytlr.. -n 10`

```
jj log -r 'ancestors(ytlr, 6) | descendants(ytlr, 5)'
```

Byte-for-byte the same ten commits, in the same order. The depth arguments count the anchor itself, so `6` is x plus 5 ancestors and `5` is x plus 4 descendants.

## Example 2: `vc-x1 list ..@----.. -n 10`

```
jj log -r 'ancestors(@----, 6) | descendants(@----, 5)'
```

Same shape, but it returns **20 commits, not 10** - and that difference is the interesting part. `@---` is the `0.78.0` trapezoid merge, so `@----` resolves to *two* commits, `ytlrkksnyzvv` and `pvolmkwprpln`, its two parents. jj gives each anchor its own 6/5 window and unions them. vc-x1 spent one global budget of 10 across the merged walk, which is why your output shows `pvol`'s ladder-side descendants above and `ytlr`'s ancestors below, ten rows total.

## So: three things revsets cannot do here

1. **You do the arithmetic.** `-n 10` becomes depth 6 and depth 5, and you have to know the split rule (n-1, ancestors take the extra). The house form computes it.
2. **`-n` is not a substitute.** jj's `-n` is applied "after revisions are filtered and reordered topologically" - it truncates from the top. It cannot center a window on an anchor, which is exactly what your `..x..` does.
3. **Direction is not expressible.** `x..` versus `..x` also chooses whether the anchor sits at top or bottom. A revset is a set; it has no such notion.

## Which means I had the fix backwards

`..x..` is not a dialect of revsets at all. It is a **centered-window display control with a budget**, and revsets are a set language - different tools that happen to collide on one spelling. Deleting the notation would delete a capability jj genuinely does not have, and no amount of `::` gets it back.

So the fix is a **re-spelling, not a retirement**: keep the affordance, stop borrowing jj's `..`. Then the positional and `-r` take real revsets verbatim, and both capabilities coexist with no ambiguity. Options worth weighing:

- **grep-style context flags**: `vc-x1 list -r ytlr -B 5 -A 4`, revset anywhere, window on flags. Most composable, since the anchor can then be any revset rather than a single symbol.
- **`--around N`**: keeps today's single-budget split behavior under an explicit name.
- **a different marker**: `~ytlr~ -n 10`, same shape, a character jj does not use.

I lean toward the first. It is the only one that lets the window apply to an arbitrary revset instead of a bare symbol, and it drops the parsing layer entirely rather than moving it.

I'll rewrite Todo #1 around this - the item stops being "adopt jj semantics" and becomes "stop colliding with jj's spelling, keep the window". That also shrinks it: no capability is lost, so the durable-text sweep and the docs rewrite are most of the work.

Two things unchanged from before: jj.md's primer still glosses `X..` wrongly and that is a template proposal, and the mailbox needs a reply, though now the correction is "the house notation is a windowing feature, not a revset dialect" rather than anything about translation layers.

**The plain version:** both of your examples do translate - `ancestors(x, N) | descendants(x, M)` - but you have to compute the depths yourself, and the second one returns 20 instead of 10 because `@----` is two commits on a merge and jj has no shared budget. The centered window with a count is a real feature revsets can't express, so we should rename it rather than remove it, and free up `..` for jj's meaning.

Want me to rewrite the entry that way before I touch anything else? And I still need those five validation commands.

## The orientation flip is the right call, and it has a precedent stronger than "jj's `..`"

jj's `..` is a poor model to copy, because `x..` there is `~::x` and has no "descendants" reading at all. The better anchor is jj's **`::` pair, which is genuinely symmetric**: `::x` ancestors, `x::` descendants. Leading marker means ancestors, trailing means descendants. Today's mapping is exactly that mirrored, so flipping lands on a rule that already exists in the tool rather than on a new house rule.

## But the flip is the most dangerous change in the item

Everything else here is additive. This one is **silent and invertible**: existing muscle memory and any script keeps parsing and returns the opposite set. Nobody gets an error, and the failure mode is a confident wrong answer - the same shape as the mailbox complaint, just aimed at ourselves.

My strong recommendation: **do not re-mean the old spelling. Kill it.** Make `x..` / `..x` / `..x..` a hard error for at least a release, with a message naming the replacement. Re-meaning it saves users one edit and costs them a class of wrong answers they cannot detect. Erroring costs one edit and is impossible to get wrong. Cheap insurance on the only genuinely breaking part of this.

## `~` is the one character you can't have

I checked jj's grammar. `~` is already jj revset syntax, in both positions:

- `~x` - "Revisions that are not in `x`" (negation)
- `x ~ y` - set difference

So `~x` meaning "ancestors of x" recreates the exact bug we are fixing, in a new character, and *worse*: `~x` is a valid revset that parses and returns a real answer, so the collision is fully silent. Suffix `x~` is safe - jj's `~` is infix and needs a right operand, so `x~` alone is a parse error there - but that only saves half the shortcut and destroys the symmetry that made it appealing.

If you want a marker, it needs a character jj's revset grammar does not use at all. `%` and `^` are both absent from jj's revset documentation. `^` carries git baggage (git's parent and exclude marker), so `%x` / `x%` / `%x%` is the one I would pick. It is ugly, which is a fair price for unambiguous.

I would also put the honest option on the table: **flags only, no marker**. `-B` / `-A` cover everything the marker does, and the marker's remaining value is saving five keystrokes on a form that has already bitten us once in this exact way.

## The `-B` / `-A` vocabulary hazard

Your output is newest-first in every case, so:

- `-B` (grep: lines *before*, printed above) = **descendants**
- `-A` (grep: lines *after*, printed below) = **ancestors**

That is coherent, and it is also a trap: someone reading "-A = after" as "later in time" gets descendants and is wrong. Document them exactly as grep does, in terms of lines above and below, and never in graph vocabulary. Then two vocabularies coexist without either lying: flags talk about the screen, revsets talk about the graph.

Two decisions to make explicitly rather than discover:

- **Both given** (`%x%` and `-B/-A`): error, don't pick a winner. Silent precedence is how the `..` mess got its footing.
- **Multi-commit anchors.** With flags the anchor can be any revset, which brings your example 2 back: `@----` is two commits. Is `-B 4` four rows total, or four per anchor? Today's budget is global. jj's depth functions are per-anchor, which is why the equivalent returned 20. Pick one and say so in the help.

## One thing that shrinks the job

For the ancestors side - almost certainly the common case - **plain revsets plus `-n` already work today**: `vc-x1 list -r '::x' -n 10` gives x and its 9 nearest ancestors, because `::x` topologically sorted puts x first. So the shortcut is really only earning its keep for the centered window and the descendants side, where `-n` truncates from the wrong end. Worth knowing before deciding how much syntax to spend.

**The plain version:** flip the orientation, yes, and use jj's `::x` / `x::` as the model rather than `..`. But make the old spelling an error instead of quietly meaning the opposite - that is the only part of this that can hurt someone silently. And `~` cannot be the shortcut: jj already uses it for "not", so `~x` would parse as a real revset and return a real wrong answer. If you want a marker, `%` is free; otherwise `-B` / `-A` alone do the whole job.

content.text:
You're right, and it breaks the hard-error idea. `..x` and `x..` are both valid jj: your own first transcript ran `jj log -r '..@'` successfully. So erroring on them is not "reject bad input", it is **refusing valid input to protect ourselves** - a permanent hole in the one thing the tool is supposed to do, pass revsets through. Drop that proposal.

## Your positional point generalizes further than you aimed it

"Could still conflict with jj if or when they allow positional revsets" is the argument that settles the marker question too, and I think it retires `%` along with `~`.

The distinction worth naming: **we own our flags; we do not own the revset language.** Any house syntax living inside the expression slot is squatting on a namespace someone else versions. `..` was squatting on an occupied lot. `~` turns out to be occupied too. `%` is a vacant lot in a subdivision jj is still building - lower probability, identical failure mode, and silent again when it lands.

Flags do not have that property. `vc-x1 list -B 4` is vc-x1's flag on vc-x1's command; nobody expects it to mean what `jj log -B` means, and jj adding a `-B` would not change what ours does. The collision surface is zero rather than small.

So my honest read is that "adopt both" should become **flags only**, and I would rather say that plainly than quietly deliver half of what you asked for. You lose the five-keystroke shortcut. You gain a positional and `-r` that are pure revsets forever, with no reserved characters and nothing to re-litigate when jj grows syntax. Given you just identified the future-conflict risk yourself, I think that trade is the one you actually want - but it is your call, and `%` remains available if the shortcut is worth the residual risk to you.

## On skipping the hard error

Agreed, and for a better reason than "only two users": the right mitigation is not a guard at all, it is the **durable-text sweep already scoped into the item**. Grepping the repos for the old forms and rewriting them in the same cycle converts this from "something we might type wrong later" to "it is already gone." A guard defends against the habit; the sweep removes it.

Two caveats on "we are the only users":

- **The bot is a user, and a literal-minded one.** It works from the instruction files, the notes and `--help`, so anything left un-swept becomes a wrong answer it produces confidently. That raises the bar on sweep thoroughness, not on error handling.
- **After the flip, `x..` starts meaning `~::x`**, which on this repo - with `config-discoverability` and `support-trapezoid-commits` parked - pulls in unrelated commits. That is precisely the hazard the mailbox opened with, now pointed at us. Another reason the sweep is the deliverable and the error is not.

## Where that leaves the design

- positional and `-r`: real revsets, verbatim to jj, no house forms, no reserved characters
- `-B` / `-A`: the window, documented in grep's vocabulary (lines above, lines below), never in ancestor/descendant terms
- `-n`: a plain limit, same as jj's
- no marker
- the flip ships with the sweep, no deprecation error, no warning

Still open from earlier and unaffected by this: whether `-B 4` on a multi-commit anchor like `@----` is four rows total or four per anchor. Today's budget is global, jj's depth functions are per-anchor, and the answer belongs in `--help` rather than in whatever the code happens to do.

**The plain version:** you are right that a hard error would refuse legitimate jj syntax, so drop it. Your worry about staking out the positional applies to any marker character, including the `%` I suggested - so I would drop the shortcut entirely and put the window on `-B`/`-A` alone, leaving the expression slot as pure jj forever. Skipping the error is fine; the sweep is what actually protects us, and it needs to cover the instruction files because the bot reads those as instructions.

content.text:
`-A`, `-B`, `-C` are all free; `CommonArgs` currently takes `-r`, `-R`, `-s`, `-n`, `-l`, `-L`.

## Agreed, and it settles two open questions

It is grep's exact trio, including `-C` as sugar for equal `-B`/`-A`. No new vocabulary for anyone who has used grep, which is the entire point.

More importantly it answers the multi-anchor question I flagged, and answers it *correctly*. `-B m -A n` on anchor `x` is precisely:

```
descendants(x, m+1) | ancestors(x, n+1)
```

which is what I ran against your two examples. So the flags are **depth limits applied per anchor**, and `@----` being two commits gives two windows unioned - the 20-row result, not a 10-row one. That is now the natural answer rather than a judgment call, it matches jj exactly, and it is one sentence in `--help`.

## What it changes, and I think for the better

`-C N` is **N per side**, so `-C 4` is 9 rows. Today's `..x.. -n 10` is a *total budget of 10*, split unevenly by a rule nobody could recall: `n-1`, halved, ancestors take the remainder. That rule is why the README has to explain that `..x.. -n 4` gives 1 descendant, x, and 2 ancestors.

I would drop the budget model entirely rather than preserve it under new flags. Per-side counts are predictable, asymmetric by construction via `-B`/`-A`, and map 1:1 onto jj's depth functions - so the implementation is a revset composition rather than a walk with an accounting rule, and the `--help` can state the exact equivalence above. The old model's only advantage was "fill exactly N rows", which is a screen-fitting concern, not a graph one.

## Two rules worth fixing now rather than discovering

**`-n` alongside the window.** There would be two limiters. Keep `-n` as jj's plain limit - applied after the set is built, truncating from the top - and say so. It composes, and it means `vc-x1 list -r x -C 4 -n 5` gives the top 5 of the 9, dropping the far ancestors. Slightly surprising, but it is exactly what "limit" means everywhere else in both tools, and inventing a rebalancing `-n` would recreate the budget rule we just deleted.

**`-C` together with `-B`/`-A`.** grep resolves this by order, which is fine for a one-shot pipeline and bad for a command someone scripts. I would make the explicit flag win regardless of order, so `-C 5 -B 1` is before 1, after 5, independent of how it was typed. Order-dependent flag semantics is the kind of thing that reads correctly and behaves otherwise.

## One naming note

Since `-B` is "before" in the printed sense, it is descendants, and `-A` is ancestors. That inversion against graph intuition is unavoidable if the output stays newest-first, and it is the right trade - but it means the `--help` text for these three flags should never contain the words "ancestor" or "descendant". Describe them as rows above and below, then give the revset equivalence once, in its own line, for people who want it. Mixing the vocabularies in the same sentence is what would make it confusing.

**The plain version:** take it as proposed. `-C N` becomes N per side rather than N total, which drops the old split-budget arithmetic and makes the flags exactly jj's depth functions - which in turn makes the multi-anchor case answer itself. Set two rules in `--help`: `-n` truncates after the window, and an explicit `-B`/`-A` beats `-C` whatever the order.

On validation: I have asked three times and you are mid-design, so I will stop asking. Unless you object, `0.79.0-0` will write those five commands into `custom.md` - `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo install --path . --locked` for full, `cargo test` for fast - and you can correct them at the working-copy review, where a wrong one fails loudly anyway.

content.text:
Yes. That is better than what I proposed, and it retires the caution I gave you one message ago.

## It removes the trap instead of documenting around it

With `-B`/`-A` the flags talk about the screen while the user thinks about the graph, so `--help` had to avoid the words "ancestor" and "descendant" to stay honest. With `-A` ancestors and `-D` descendants there is nothing to avoid: the flags say what they mean, and `--help` can use the graph vocabulary freely because that is now the vocabulary the flags are in.

The rows do not even change. Under newest-first output, grep's `-A` (after, printed below) *is* ancestors, and `-B` (before, printed above) *is* descendants. So `-A` keeps both its letter and its exact behavior while shedding a misleading justification, and `-D` replaces `-B` with the same rows under a name that explains them.

## The letters line up with the implementation

```
-D m -A n   ->   descendants(x, m+1) | ancestors(x, n+1)
```

The flag letters are now the first letters of the jj functions they compile to. That equivalence goes straight into `--help` as one line and needs no gloss.

## And it survives a change we might make later

`-B`/`-A` are only correct *because* output is newest-first. Add a `--reverse` someday and they silently inverte relative to the graph - the same silent-inversion failure that started this whole thread, rebuilt in fresh flags. `-A`/`-D` are defined against the DAG, so ordering can change underneath them and they stay true. Worth having, given the topic.

## Two small follow-ons

**Long forms**: `--ancestors N`, `--descendants N`, `--centered N`, so `--help` and scripts read plainly and `-C` keeps a name that still makes sense once "context" is no longer the metaphor.

**Resist adding `-B` as an alias.** Someone will want it for grep muscle memory, and a second spelling for the same thing is precisely the species of decision that produced the `..` collision. One spelling per concept - the same rule this whole discussion has been enforcing on the revset side, applied to our own flags.

**The plain version:** `-A` ancestors, `-D` descendants, `-C` both. Same rows as the grep trio, honest names, letters matching `ancestors()` and `descendants()`, and correct even if the display order ever changes. Take it.

content.text:
Your diagnosis is sharper than the fix it produced. The flaw was not picking the wrong rotation, it was that a rotation was load-bearing at all. A spatial metaphor has a free parameter, so it can only be learned by being told. "Ancestor" has no free parameter, so it can be derived. That is the whole reason `-A`/`-D` is better, stated generally.

But I don't think the counter-clockwise version saves us. Work it through: `..x` would have meant ancestors, agreeing with jj. `x..` would have meant descendants, and jj's `x..` is `~::x`. So one form matches and one still silently disagrees.

That is the worse outcome, not the better one. Today the collision is total, which is why your two `vc-x1 list` runs made it obvious in about ten seconds. Half-agreement is the version that survives for years: the form you test first works, so you trust the other one, and it quietly returns a different set on a repo with parked bookmarks. We would still be having this conversation, just later and with a bug attached instead of a design discussion.

So the coin flip was never the problem. `..` meant "which way do I walk from here", jj's `..` means "which commits are in this set", and no rotation reconciles a walk with a set.

(No apology needed on the detail. You were making a point that needed the setup, and I'm the last one who gets to complain.)

**The plain version:** you are right about the cause, wrong about the escape. Getting the rotation right would have hidden half the mismatch instead of fixing it, which is worse than the obvious break we actually got.

# custom.md - vc-x1's project layer

The one agent-editable instruction file (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd-the-project-layer)).
Loaded after AGENTS.md; on conflict, this file wins.

## Medium and validation

A Rust CLI. Manifest `Cargo.toml`, package `vc-x1-dev`; the version-of-record is its `version`
field, with `Cargo.lock` its derived copy (`cargo update -p vc-x1-dev --offline` after a bump).
The installed dogfood binary is `vc-x1-dev`; see [Dev artifact name](agent-data/versioning.md).

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 5; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
  - four separate invocations, each exit status checked before the next:
    - `cargo fmt`
    - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    - `cargo test`
    - `cargo install --path . --locked`
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - `cargo test`

Never pipe a validating command into `tail` / `grep` and then `&&` the next one: the pipeline's
status is the last stage's, so the gate is decorative (found at the `0.77.0` close-out). Use
`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` when a pipe is genuinely wanted.

## Project conventions and overrides

- **Invoke `vc-x1-dev`, never `vc-x1`.** The dogfood binary is what this repo builds and what
  its changes must be exercised against; `vc-x1` is whatever happens to be installed.
- **Mailbox parameters**: member name `vc-x1`; the template repository is at
  `../vc-x1-template` (mailbox `messages/vc-x1.md` there, protocol in its `MESSAGES.md`).
  Provisional: an open proposal moves these to `.vc-config.toml`, on the grounds that they are
  environment configuration rather than instruction text and custom.md should be generic at
  birth (mailbox, 2026-08-03).

# Chores-16

Continuation of `chores-15.md` (closed after `0.78.0`, the jj-lib migration close-out; the
`0.78.1` instruction-set interlude between the files is recorded in its TODO.md program-ladder
rung and commit body). This file covers `0.78.2` onward, back on `main` with the refactor
program's long-lived bookmark retired and the 20260803 baseline pin set in force.

Reference numbering is file-local; see
[`agent-data/notes.md`](../../agent-data/notes.md#reference-numbering); chores-16 starts at
`[1]`.

## Table of Contents

- [style: typeable punctuation + line-width source sweep](#style-typeable-punctuation--line-width-source-sweep)

## style: typeable punctuation + line-width source sweep

- [[1]] 0.78.2 style: typeable punctuation + line-width source sweep

`src/` + `tests/` predate the typeable-punctuation rule and code.md's <=100-col comment wrap:
863 banned-character sites across 63 files and 60 overlong lines at pickup. A single-commit
cycle (wink's call at the opening review: the sweep is one homogeneous transformation, so a
ladder would checkpoint nothing a review gate and jj's op log don't already cover).

- the four named characters went to zero: `->` and `...` by mechanical replace, the 708 em
  dashes each given their structural decision (colon for term-elaboration, comma for
  continuation, parentheses for asides, sentence splits for contrasts), converted by four
  parallel lesser-model agents on disjoint file batches and audited after
- the sweep surfaced four *more* untypeable species the ban list does not name: `=>` was
  written `⇒` (13 sites), the config/show output drew rules with `─` (56), plus one `≥` and
  one U+2212 minus; all converted, output tests updated in the same pass (see the dogfood
  finding on the enumeration)
- the ellipsis in `truncate_chars` was load-bearing: appending one-char `…` kept truncated
  gists at cap+1, and the mechanical `...` conversion broke the length test; the function now
  reserves room for the suffix and stays within `max` (contract tightened, test to `<= CAP`)
- `config_cmd` section headers (`# ── x ──`) and `show`'s separator rule are user-visible
  output; they render as `-` runs now, and the README's config samples were regenerated from
  the installed binary so the docs match what the code emits
- line width: string literals split with backslash continuation (content byte-identical),
  comments re-wrapped, trailing `// OK:` comments moved above their statement where wrapping
  was awkward; exempt as literal rows: the JSONL fixture strings in the transcript /
  bot-session tests, and comment URLs

Riding in the same commit: the cycle records, the Done-retirement sweep of four
refactor-program entries into done.md, the `0.78.1` ladder-ref backfill, and the first
generic-custom.md-test findings logged in [notes/dogfood.md](../dogfood.md).

### Delegation notes

Four Sonnet agents converted the em-dash batches and a fifth did the line-width pass; two
incidents worth remembering when delegating sweeps:

- one batch agent "corrected" scope creep it thought it saw, reverting 29 already-converted
  arrows back to `→` because it compared against a pre-sweep baseline; caught by the
  post-batch character audit. A delegated sweep needs the invariant stated as "the end state
  is X", not "convert only Y": agents infer baselines
- the line-width agent first placed the continuation break-space after the backslash, which
  Rust strips with the leading whitespace, silently corrupting a fixture string; its own
  `cargo test` run caught it. String splits verify by test, not by eye

# References

[1]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/a8b43a18999e "a8b43a18999ece30e7b807650ba45eb9b236ebdc"

## refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation

- [[N]] 0.79.0-0 refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation opening

The trapezoid close-out is a four-step manual recipe, and its warts are all artifacts of the
shape having no command: an interim published shape, a sideways bookmark move, a backfill
embargo window. `vc-x1 trapezoid-push` makes it first-party, as a subcommand rather than a flag
on `push`, so `push` keeps a stateable invariant: it never produces a merge. Body-intro
validation rides as the first rung, turning jj's opaque `-m "-..."` arg-parse failure
([bugs.md](../bugs.md) #7) into a clear error naming the offending line. The last rung of the
jj-lib refactor program; at this close-out the program's `## In Progress` block retires here.

### 0.79.0-0 refactor: trapezoid-push + body-intro validation opening

Cycle open, plus the records work the previous push left outstanding.

- the `0.78.0` and `0.78.2` as-built rungs were both still `[[N]]`, each being its cycle's
  close-out, which nothing inside that cycle can backfill; the accompanying dogfood entry
  proposes a greppable acceptance check rather than a per-file recall
- the parked `support-trapezoid-commits` bookmark is scheduled for deletion rather than
  rebasing: its one commit extracts `push/state.rs`, the module `0.77.0` deleted, so the
  quarry the disposition note anticipated has no ore in it. The `0.72.0-0` chore commit is
  abandoned with it
- `custom.md` gains its first real content since the `0.78.1` reset to the bare skeleton: the
  validation commands, the dogfood-binary rule, and the mailbox parameters, all three named as
  missing by the generic-custom.md test's first findings
- the `por -> dual conversion` stage leaves the refactor program for its own `## Todo`. It is
  init/setup work, its stated dependencies (facade topology, the in-process init pieces) have
  both shipped, and holding a program open for one independent feature buys nothing
- the revset item was rescoped at wink's review: it is not a translation layer to switch off
  (`resolve_revset` already passes verbatim to jj), but a house `..` notation that inverts
  jj's. It becomes its own cycle after this one, adopting jj's notation and moving the
  windowing to `-A` / `-D` / `-C` flags

# References
